title: Materials in Objects
description: Objects are made of one or more materials. The materials chosen for an object depend on the properties needed — strength, flexibility, or waterproofing.

exercises.question: A bicycle frame is made of METAL. Why is metal a good choice?
exercises.exp: Metal is strong and durable — perfect for a bike frame that needs to support a rider safely.

exercises.question: A raincoat is made of WATERPROOF material. Why?
choices: to keep rain out and keep you dry
because it is the cheapest material
exercises.exp: Waterproof materials repel water — essential for staying dry in the rain!

exercises.question: A GLASS WINDOW is made of glass. What property makes glass good for windows?
choices: it is transparent so you can see through it
exercises.exp: Glass is transparent — light passes through and you can see outside. Perfect for windows!

exercises.question: Which object uses MORE THAN ONE material?
choices: a running shoe (rubber sole, fabric upper, metal eyelets)
exercises.exp: Running shoes use rubber for grip, fabric for comfort, and metal eyelets for laces — multiple materials!

exercises.question: Why are CUTTING BOARDS made of wood or plastic instead of paper?
choices: wood and plastic are more durable and easy to clean
exercises.exp: Wood and plastic are strong, waterproof, and easy to sanitise — paper would get soggy and fall apart.

exercises.question: A RUBBER BAND can stretch and return to its shape. This property is called ___.
exercises.exp: Elasticity means a material can stretch and bounce back to its original shape.

exercises.question: Which property makes WOOL a good material for winter mittens?
choices: it is an insulator that traps warm air
exercises.exp: Wool traps warm air in its fibres, keeping your hands warm in cold weather!

exercises.question: A FRYING PAN has a metal pan and a plastic handle. Why is the handle plastic?
choices: plastic is a poor conductor of heat — the handle stays cool
exercises.exp: Plastic does not conduct heat well, so the handle stays cool while the metal pan gets hot.

exercises.question: Which material would be BEST for making a boat that floats?
choices: lightweight waterproof materials like fibreglass or sealed wood
exercises.exp: Boats are made of lightweight, waterproof materials so they can float and stay dry inside.

exercises.question: A CONCRETE BUILDING uses steel rods inside the concrete walls. Why?
choices: steel adds strength and prevents cracking
exercises.exp: Steel rods (rebar) inside concrete add tensile strength — concrete is strong under pressure but weak under pulling forces.

exercises.question: Glass is FRAGILE. What does fragile mean?
choices: it can break easily when dropped or hit
exercises.exp: Fragile means something breaks easily. Glass shatters when dropped — handle with care!

exercises.question: Why do SURGEONS use stainless steel scalpels instead of plastic ones?
choices: stainless steel stays sharp, is durable, and can be sterilised
plastic cannot be made in scalpel shapes
exercises.exp: Stainless steel stays razor-sharp, resists rust, and can be sterilised in high heat — essential for surgery.

exercises.question: A trampoline is made of a STRETCHY fabric mat. What property is most important here?
choices: elasticity — the ability to stretch and return to shape
exercises.exp: A trampoline mat must be elastic — it stretches under a jumper's weight then springs back, launching them upward!

exercises.question: Why is COPPER used to make electrical wires?
choices: it is a good conductor of electricity
exercises.exp: Copper conducts electricity extremely well — electrons flow through it easily. That is why wires, circuits, and power cables are copper!

exercises.question: BUBBLE WRAP is used to protect fragile items when shipping. Which TWO properties make it useful?
exercises.exp: Bubble wrap is light (doesn't add much weight) and cushions objects by absorbing shocks — perfect for fragile packaging!

exercises.question: A LIFE JACKET is filled with foam. Why is foam a good material for a life jacket?
choices: foam is dense and sinks in water
foam is lightweight and traps air — making it buoyant
exercises.exp: Foam is full of trapped air bubbles — it is very lightweight and floats, keeping the wearer above water!

exercises.question: SUNSCREEN is applied to skin. What key property must sunscreen have?
choices: it must be transparent and absorb UV light
it must be solid at all temperatures
exercises.exp: Sunscreen must be transparent (so you can't see it) and must absorb or reflect harmful UV rays to protect skin.

exercises.question: A TENT is made of nylon fabric. What two properties are most important?
exercises.exp: A good tent must be waterproof (to keep rain out) and lightweight (easy to carry while hiking or camping).

exercises.question: CERAMICS (like pottery and tiles) are used for floors and dishes. What key property do they have?
choices: they are hard, heat-resistant, and do not react with food or chemicals
exercises.exp: Ceramics are very hard, heat-resistant, non-reactive, and easy to clean — perfect for tiles, mugs, and dishes!

exercises.question: A HOCKEY HELMET has a hard outer shell and soft foam inside. Why TWO materials?
choices: hard shell spreads impact; foam absorbs energy — both protect the head differently
exercises.exp: The hard shell distributes force widely; the foam absorbs and slows the impact — working together for maximum protection.

exercises.question: AEROGEL is the world's lightest solid material. It is an excellent INSULATOR. What would it be good for?
choices: insulating buildings or spacesuits — keeping heat in or out
exercises.exp: Aerogel is incredibly light and traps air in tiny pores — it is one of the best insulators known and is used in buildings and Mars rovers!

exercises.question: A CAST IRON pan is heavy but holds heat well. A thin aluminium pan heats quickly but cools fast. Which is better for slow-cooking stews?
exercises.exp: Cast iron stores thermal energy well — it heats evenly and holds heat a long time, perfect for slow cooking.

exercises.question: CARBON FIBRE is used in racing bicycles. It is stronger than steel but much lighter. Why does this matter?
choices: colour is more important than weight
a lighter, stronger frame means the cyclist uses less energy to go faster
exercises.exp: In racing, every gram matters — carbon fibre gives extreme strength without the mass penalty of steel, making bikes faster!

exercises.question: SAFETY GOGGLES are made of clear, shatter-resistant plastic. What TWO properties are needed?
exercises.exp: Safety goggles must be transparent (to see through) and tough enough not to shatter when hit by debris or chemicals.

exercises.question: A BRIDGE CABLE must support enormous weight. What property is most important?
choices: high tensile strength — able to withstand stretching forces without breaking
exercises.exp: Bridge cables (usually steel wires) need tremendous tensile strength to hold the weight of the bridge and traffic without snapping.

exercises.question: Why are RUBBER GLOVES used when working with electricity?
choices: rubber is an insulator that stops electricity from passing through to the hands
exercises.exp: Rubber does not conduct electricity — it insulates your hands, preventing electric current from passing through and shocking you.

exercises.question: What does BIODEGRADABLE mean for a material?
choices: it can be broken down naturally by organisms into harmless substances
exercises.exp: Biodegradable materials (like paper or food scraps) are broken down by bacteria and fungi — returning to nature without harming the environment.

exercises.question: Plastics are made from OIL (a non-renewable resource). What is one advantage of using PLANT-BASED plastics instead?
choices: they are stronger than regular plastic
they use a renewable resource and can biodegrade
exercises.exp: Plant-based plastics use renewable resources (corn, sugarcane) and many can biodegrade — better for a circular, sustainable economy.

exercises.question: SANDPAPER is used to smooth wood. What property of sandpaper makes it effective?
choices: its surface is rough and abrasive — scratching away the surface material
exercises.exp: Sandpaper is covered in tiny hard grit (like silicon carbide). The abrasive roughness scratches and smooths wood surfaces.

exercises.question: Scientists test a new material and find it is strong, lightweight, AND flexible. This material would be BEST for making ___.
exercises.exp: Strong + lightweight + flexible = ideal for body armour or sports protection — needing to absorb impacts without adding bulk.

exercises.question: When engineers choose materials for a product, they must consider ___.
choices: only the colour of the material
the properties of the material AND the requirements of the product
only how the material looks under a microscope
exercises.exp: Good material selection matches the material's properties (strength, flexibility, conductivity) to what the product actually needs to do.

exercises.question: COMPOSITE materials combine two or more materials. Fibreglass (glass + plastic resin) is stronger than either material alone. Why do engineers create composites?
choices: to combine the best properties of multiple materials into one superior material
to make materials cheaper to destroy
composites are only used in art
exercises.exp: Composites are engineered to get the best of both worlds — fibreglass is light like plastic AND strong like glass. Aircraft, boats, and car parts use composites!

exercises.question: Steel is an ALLOY of iron and carbon. An alloy is ___.
choices: a mixture of two or more metals (or a metal and another element) with improved properties
exercises.exp: Alloys combine metals to create superior materials. Steel is stronger than pure iron; bronze (copper + tin) is harder than copper alone!

exercises.question: Why is COPPER used for electrical wiring in houses?
choices: copper is magnetic and attracts electricity
copper is an excellent conductor of electricity and is flexible enough to be drawn into thin wires
copper is the cheapest metal available
exercises.exp: Copper is chosen for wiring because it conducts electricity excellently AND is ductile (can be drawn into wires). It is the ideal electrical conductor!

exercises.question: A BIODEGRADABLE material is one that ___.
choices: can be broken down naturally by bacteria and other organisms
exercises.exp: Biodegradable materials decompose naturally — like paper, cotton, and food scraps. Non-biodegradable plastics can last hundreds of years in landfills!

exercises.question: Why is GLASS used for windows instead of wood or metal?
choices: glass is transparent, allowing light in while keeping wind and rain out
glass is the cheapest available material
exercises.exp: Glass is perfect for windows — it is transparent (lets light through), hard, weatherproof, and can be made very flat and smooth.

exercises.question: A THERMAL INSULATOR slows down the transfer of heat. Which is the best thermal insulator?
exercises.exp: Glass wool and foam trap air in tiny pockets — air is a very poor conductor of heat, making these materials excellent insulators for buildings!

exercises.question: The TENSILE STRENGTH of a material is ___.
choices: its ability to resist being pulled apart (stretched)
exercises.exp: Tensile strength measures resistance to being pulled apart. Steel cables on bridges need enormous tensile strength to hold the load!

exercises.question: Which statement about SMART MATERIALS is correct?
choices: smart materials have fixed properties that never change
smart materials change their properties in response to changes in environment (heat, light, electricity)
only electronic devices use smart materials
smart materials have no practical uses
exercises.exp: Smart materials respond to stimuli — shape-memory alloys return to their original shape when heated, photochromic glass darkens in sunlight!

exercises.question: POLYMERS are long chain molecules. Which everyday material is a polymer?
exercises.exp: Polymers are long repeating molecular chains. Synthetic polymers include nylon and polyethylene (plastic bags). Natural polymers include silk, wool, and DNA!

exercises.question: Sand and gravel are used to make CONCRETE. Concrete is ___.
choices: a composite material made from cement, water, sand, and gravel
exercises.exp: Concrete is a composite — cement binds sand and gravel together when mixed with water and hardened. It is one of the most widely used construction materials!

exercises.question: A material's DENSITY determines whether it floats or sinks in water. Objects LESS DENSE than water ___.
exercises.exp: Objects less dense than water (density < 1 g/cm³) float — wood, cork, and most plastics float. Objects denser than water (like steel) sink.

exercises.question: STAINLESS STEEL is used for kitchen equipment and medical tools because ___.
choices: it is strong, hard, resistant to rust and corrosion, and easy to sterilise
it is the only material that does not conduct heat
exercises.exp: Stainless steel resists rust (due to added chromium), is strong, and can be sterilised — perfect for scalpels, sinks, and cutlery!

exercises.question: Which material would BEST replace a cracked ceramic bathroom tile?
choices: another ceramic tile — matching properties of hardness, water resistance, and appearance
exercises.exp: Replacing materials requires matching properties. A ceramic tile needs hardness, water resistance, and a matching appearance — so another ceramic tile!

exercises.question: Aerogel is a material that is 99.8% air. It is an EXCELLENT insulator and extremely LIGHT. What is its best use?
choices: thermal insulation in space suits and buildings — lightweight yet superb insulator
exercises.exp: Aerogel — made mostly of air — is the world's lightest solid and an extraordinary thermal insulator. NASA uses it in Mars rover insulation!

exercises.question: When choosing a material for a PARACHUTE, which TWO properties are most important?
choices: strong AND lightweight — it must hold the weight of a person but not add too much mass itself
exercises.exp: A parachute needs strength (to support a person's weight) AND lightweight material (so it deploys easily and the user can carry it). Nylon is ideal!

exercises.question: RECYCLING aluminium cans saves energy because ___.
choices: recycling aluminium uses about 95% less energy than producing new aluminium from raw ore (bauxite)
exercises.exp: Extracting aluminium from bauxite ore requires enormous energy (electrolysis). Recycling uses 95% less energy — huge environmental and economic savings!

exercises.question: A material is said to be BRITTLE if it ___.
choices: returns to its original shape when force is removed
breaks or shatters suddenly with little deformation
stretches a long way before breaking
exercises.exp: Brittle materials (glass, ceramics, cast iron) break suddenly without much bending. Ductile materials (steel, copper) stretch before breaking.

exercises.question: The MOHS HARDNESS SCALE ranks minerals from 1 (softest) to 10 (hardest). A mineral that SCRATCHES glass (hardness 5.5) has a hardness ___.
exercises.exp: A harder mineral scratches a softer one. If it scratches glass (5.5), its hardness must be greater than 5.5. Diamond (10) is the hardest!

exercises.question: Why is CARBON FIBRE used in Formula 1 racing cars?
choices: it is magnetic and responds to steering
it is exceptionally strong and VERY lightweight — making cars faster and safer
it is the cheapest material available
it is transparent, helping the driver see better
exercises.exp: Carbon fibre has an incredible strength-to-weight ratio — stronger than steel but much lighter. Less weight = more speed and better fuel efficiency!

exercises.question: Which property of RUBBER makes it ideal for car tyres?
choices: rubber is transparent and allows light through
rubber is elastic and provides good grip (friction) on road surfaces
exercises.exp: Rubber's elasticity absorbs road bumps AND its high friction with road surfaces provides the grip needed for braking and cornering!

exercises.question: A packaging company wants eco-friendly material that breaks down naturally after disposal. They should choose ___.
exercises.exp: Mycelium (fungal) packaging decomposes naturally within weeks. It is grown from agricultural waste and is a genuinely sustainable packaging alternative!
